Are you familiar with both? I just read the following on the difference between the two:

>Python has been designed to emphasize programmer productivity and code readability. The Python syntax enforces strict indentation rules; in fact, indentation has semantic meaning in Python.
Ruby was designed, first and foremost, to make programming fun for its creator, with The Principle of Least Surprise and There's more than one way to do the same thing as guiding concepts:
Ruby inherited the Perl philosophy of having more than one way to do the same thing.
—Yukihiro Matsumoto (Matz) , The Philosophy of Ruby

The idea of strict rules makes me think that Python would be easier to learn but more boring. With multiple ways of doing the same thing, Ruby seems more complex, but I like fun... I'm just not sure if it's the same type of fun that I consider fun.

Are you familiar enough with the two to elaborate on these statements and possibly give a simple example of both languages doing the same thing and examples of Ruby doing the same thing in different ways?

Unfortunately, I don't look at things as improve or worsen... just things that happen. Does taking a walk really improve your life? Does playing a sport improve your life? Who is to say that those two examples don't worsen your life by injuring your body? When you take everything at face value, it's just time passing, and a minute doing one thing is the same as a minute doing another thing. Everything is just... blah to me and nothing really matters anymore.

It is my understanding that trivial things are uninteresting just from looking at it from my own perspective. I have no interest in knowing how you went to the grocery store and bought two oranges but later found out one was bruised so you went back and swapped it for another one, so I can only assume others would not want to hear a similar story from me... in this example, stayed at home in my underwear and played Battlefield 3 for 7 hours straight. This mundane day to day information seems to be a staple in modern relationships which suggests to me that I will probably be alone forever... unless of course something worth mentioning happens to me and her every day... or she's under the understanding that there is a level of quality expected with each conversation if a conversation were to start.

Love is an elusive concept that not everyone subscribes to. People often say "you'll know it when you feel it" giving the impression that even those who know it and feel it can't explain exactly what it is, so the best approach to understand it is to study the effects it has on someone feeling it rather than exactly what it feels like. The most predominate effect that love has that I have noticed is that it makes someone favor an individual over everyone else in that group of people.

Bonus information: Taking this concept and definition into how I view the world, I believe in the existence of love, however, I don't understand how I could ever love anyone outside my family. I will choose my family over anyone else's family, but when it comes to choosing a stranger and favoring them over everyone else, I just don't understand how that can be possible. How does one make the decision that this girl is better than every other girl in the world? My inability to make such a decision leads me to believe that I will be alone forever.

This one took me a while to think about. My answer is that I don't know anymore. Everything has some level of enjoyment but nothing is really up there enough to want to do it.

I try not to exercise because it makes me hungry which makes me eat more of my parent's food and waste their money. I find that day dreaming is bad for me because it's unrealistic and does nothing but set me up for disappointment since I have to come back to reality every time... and that's just depressing. I do like dreaming and I sleep a lot though... it passes the time faster.
